issue.title: Host completion refuses an unchanged prepared-completion intent with stale_worktree_fingerprint after a passing check

task_type_fields.impact: A cross-repository prepared completion that verified green is refused at host time, so the agent must spend another turn on a fresh final declaration. Each failed host completion also wastes a 30-minute check.
task_type_fields.repro:
Proposed by phase sase-1pj.6.1.8 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note #3, 2026-11-01) and filed by the sase-1pj.6.1 land agent.

Repro (observed once, on athena, 2026-11-01):
1. A phase agent ran prepared-completion verification through `sase monitor start -f` (monitor enf0k7gv43fc). ToolRun adb747113d22e2940ce5234246ab2cca (`just check`) succeeded: exit 0, evidence complete, mutated_input=false, dirty 19 -> 19.
2. Host completion then refused intent `file:explicit:37585a8fa70d95de4d42d2e8` with `stale_worktree_fingerprint`.
3. The recovery agent compared every dirty-file hash, the dirty path set, and HEAD in both repositories (main and linked sase-core) against the passing check fingerprints (main adb747113d22e2940ce5234246ab2cca, core 36675320b763570dc3c9150d51007654). All matched. Current `observe_completion_repositories` output also matched the sealed main and sase-core observations exactly, including index trees, modes, content hashes, and protection flags.
4. No source edits were needed. The phase completed only through a fresh final declaration.

The refusal code is in sase-core `crates/sase_core/src/continuation/completion_eval.rs` (stale_worktree_fingerprint). The sase-side recovery surface is `src/sase/monitor/followup_prompt.py`. The root cause is unconfirmed. Candidates are a fingerprint computed over a different repository set or scope than the sealed observation (for example, the cross-repo prepared intent covering both main and sase-core), or a time-of-check difference between seal and host evaluation.

issue.creation_reason: Phase sase-1pj.6.1.8 lost a passing prepared-completion check to a fingerprint refusal even though every observed repository fingerprint matched, and it needed a manual fresh final declaration.

payload.entry: Fixed by epic sase-1sd phase .5. Confirmed mechanism: monitor members were created without prev_artifacts_dir, so baseline inheritance captured the starter's authored dirt as pre-existing protected/foreign paths. The host-time protection flags then differed from the sealed intent and refused green checks (a recorded-input replay of 3sefkg2pq2cg went eligible to ineligible on the protection flags alone). Sase commit a49dac15ca threads starter_artifacts_dir through create_monitor_member and adds a lifecycle regression (tests/monitor/test_monitor_member.py). Sase-core 6111b9b5 adds bounded per-component fingerprint mismatch diagnostics, which now reach the recovery receipt and prompt. The fail-closed refusal for real mismatches is unchanged. The older historical refusals lacked retained host-time observations, so their exact components remain unknown. Any future refusal now names its differing component, so a recurrence should be filed as a new bead with that diagnostic.
